name: Creamy White Sauce Vegetable Spaghetti
summary: Creamy cheddar white-sauce spaghetti with brown button mushrooms, capsicum, sweet corn and garlic.

preparation.after: Slice 4–5 mm thick; do not peel. Dry well to help the mushrooms brown instead of steam.
Remove the stalk, seeds and membrane. Cut about 3–4 cm long and 5–7 mm thick.
Frozen sweet corn can be used directly.
The tested guidance was approximately 3–4 large cloves.

Keep a whisk ready to make the sauce without lumps.

cookingMethod.after: Let the strands soften, gently push them into the water and stir to prevent sticking. Start checking around 9 minutes and cook according to the packet, approximately 9–11 minutes, until just tender with slight firmness.
Drain the spaghetti without rinsing or adding oil. Keep the water aside only for consistency adjustment.

cookingMethod.after: Sauté 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until released moisture mostly evaporates and the mushrooms begin to brown lightly. Avoid overcrowding the pan.
Sauté for 2–3 minutes; the capsicum should retain a slight bite.
Sauté for 30–45 seconds until fragrant, without browning. Transfer the vegetables to a plate.

cookingMethod.after: Do not let the butter brown.
Stir continuously for 1–1½ minutes until the paste is smooth, pale and lightly bubbly, without browning.
Add in 4–5 small batches, whisking smooth after each. Simmer on low-medium heat for 3–5 minutes, stirring often, until lightly thickened but still pourable.

cookingMethod.lead: If the sauce is too thick, gradually use:
cookingMethod.after: Add a little at a time, up to the reserved amount. Stop once the sauce coats the spaghetti smoothly and remains creamy, not watery.

cookingMethod.text: Switch off the heat and serve immediately. The sauce will thicken as it cools.

servingSuggestions: Serve hot as a complete main dish for 2 people × 1 meal.
Distribute the mushrooms and vegetables evenly; the sauce should cling to the spaghetti rather than pool.
notes: Finalized after the user reported that the 145 g spaghetti and 200 g brown button mushroom batch tasted good on 8 November 2026.
The 1× base deliberately keeps the full 200 g mushrooms rather than proportionally reducing them with the spaghetti.
Milk is 360 ml for this tested ratio; reserved pasta water is optional and must not be added automatically.
The tested 1× amounts for black pepper powder and mixed herbs were ⅜ teaspoon each; the site's normal practical spoon formatter may round their on-screen quantities.
Sauté mushrooms until their released moisture has mostly evaporated; add garlic only toward the end.
Keep the flour-butter paste pale and whisk milk in gradually to avoid lumps.
Cheese goes in off the heat. Start with ¼ teaspoon fine salt and add the remaining ¼ teaspoon only after tasting.
